title: ALLMod: Exploring Area-Efficiency of LUT-based Large Number Modular Reduction via Hybrid Workloads
problem: Cryptographic applications (homomorphic encryption, zero-knowledge proofs) require high-bit-width modular reduction (128–8192 bits), which is compute-intensive. LUT-based approaches reduce computation via lookup tables but incur significant hardware area overhead due to extensive LUT storage.
motivation: Emerging applications (HE, ZKP) demand large-bit-width cryptography; area efficiency is critical for practical ASIC/FPGA deployment.
method: ALLMod reduces the hardware area required for LUT-based modular reduction by splitting the computation into two balanced workloads, inspired by iterative reduction. A template fairly distributes the work between them. The system explores different timing options for combining results from both workloads to find the optimal approach. By trading computation across the two workloads this way, ALLMod shrinks the total number of lookup tables needed while maintaining throughput.
key_novelty: Hybrid workload decomposition—splitting the computation into two balanced parts—reduces the hardware area required without sacrificing computation speed.
contributions: Hybrid workload approach to LUT-based modular reduction
DSE for optimal result fusion timing
1.65× area efficiency improvement (128-bit), 3× improvement (8192-bit) vs. conventional LUT methods
limitations: Evaluation on specific bit-widths (128, 8192); applicability to non-power-of-2 bit-widths; integration with modern cryptographic libraries; power/thermal analysis not discussed.
primary_theme: hybrid-workload LUT optimization for area-efficient large-number modular reduction
